name: 360VOT
description: 360° images can provide an omnidirectional field of view which is important for stable and long-term scene perception. In this paper, we explore 360° images for visual object tracking and perceive new challenges caused by large distortion, stitching artifacts, and other unique attributes of 360° images. To alleviate these problems, we take advantage of novel representations of target localization, i.e., bounding field-of-view, and then introduce a general 360 tracking framework that can adopt typical trackers for omnidirectional tracking. More importantly, we propose a new large-scale omnidirectional tracking benchmark dataset, 360VOT, in order to facilitate future research. 360VOT contains 120 sequences with up to 113K high-resolution frames in equirectangular projection. The tracking targets cover 32 categories in diverse scenarios. evaluation_method: success rate and tracking metrics such as precision/robustness/accuracy under omnidirectional tracking protocols
reputation: A specialized tracking benchmark for 360° omnidirectional video that is useful for research but not yet a broadly standardized benchmark.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark with challenging distortion and stitching artifacts; results depend on tracker adaptation and the specific 360° evaluation protocol.
